processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting, cast into ingot
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melted in a vacuum induction furnace under argon atmosphere and cast into ingot.

processing_steps.method: solution treatment (heating + isothermal holding) and water quench
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: HR plates heated to 1050 °C, isothermally held for 0.5 h, quenched in water.
CR sheets to 3 mm thickness; this is the parent CR state shared by all DP specimens.
CR sheets annealed at 950 °C for 1 min; defines state label DP950-1 (XXX = annealing temperature, Y = period).
After annealing the specimens were quenched in water again.

structures.overall_structure: Austenite (FCC) matrix containing two types of ferrite — granular α ferrite grains and banded δ ferrite elongated along RD — in a partially recrystallized condition; shear bands retained from cold rolling. Annealing at 950 °C for 1 min produces the coarsest δ and α grains together with a large ferrite amount, and cracks are easily initiated at the α/γ interfaces.

phases_present.morphology: partially recrystallized (mixed yellow and red/pink GROD regions with heavy black boundary network)

microstructure_list.region: granular grains at austenite grain boundaries / triple points
banded, elongated along the rolling direction (RD)

phases_present.morphology: banded, elongated along RD (abundant red banded ferrite in the phase map)

defect_interactions.interaction_type: crack initiation and propagation at/along ferrite–austenite interfaces
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: The presence of a large amount of ferrite in DP950–1 causes incompatible straining at many interfaces between ferrite and the unRexed austenite due to the great difference in their strength/hardness, leading to easy initiation and propagation of cracks at/along the interfaces; therefore DP950–1 has poor ductility.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone-shaped tensile specimens with a gage length of 25 mm, length direction along the rolling direction (RD)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests; three tensile measurements were made for each heat treatment condition and the average values taken.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Phase (PH) mappings and grain-reference-orientation-deviation (GROD) mappings of austenite; dark lines are high-angle grain boundaries >15°; 20 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: To determine phase fractions (α and δ ferrite by EBSD) and the recrystallized austenite fraction (GROD < 2°)
characterization_methods.key_findings: DP950-1 phase map shows abundant red banded ferrite elongated along RD in a blue FCC matrix with a 'shear bands' label; GROD map shows mixed yellow and red/pink regions with a heavy black boundary network, indicating partial recrystallization (Rex-γ fraction 19.4%; α 19.6%, δ 9.8%).

characterization_methods.purpose: To identify phase constituents and determine the ferrite fraction
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the annealing series (5 min), FCC and BCC peaks are present throughout, with BCC peaks strongest at 900 °C and carbides appearing at 950–1000 °C; the ferrite fraction by XRD for DP950-1 is not reported ('-').

unmapped_findings: Specific yield strength (SYS) of DP950-1 = 159.6 ± 0.8 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ (Table 1, b0019).
Specific ultimate tensile strength (SUTS) of DP950-1 = 226.4 ± 1.6 MPa·g⁻¹·cm³ (Table 1, b0019).
DP950–1 has the highest ultimate tensile strength (UTS) but the lowest total elongation (TE) among the annealed specimens (b0025).

The large ferrite content of DP950–1 (and DP950–5) causes incompatible straining at the many ferrite/unRexed austenite interfaces, leading to easy crack initiation and propagation and hence poor ductility (b0025).
The engineering stress-strain curve of DP950-1 (black curve) rises steeply and terminates below about 7 % strain (Fig. 3a, figure_003).

In the SUTS-vs-TE comparison plot, DP950-1 lies among the 'Our steel' red-star data points (labelled DP950-1) clustered at the top-right, though it is not beyond the 8 GPa·g⁻¹·cm³·% contour (Fig. 3b, figure_003).
The DP950-1 specimen retains shear bands from cold rolling, as labelled in its EBSD phase map (Fig. 2b1, figure_002).
